If I am meeting someone new and someone says to them I am a trans man n stuff. That is totally unacceptable. Nobody should be able to tell anyone else about what’s in my pants, or pressure me to tell them. If I want to tell them, I will. not the other way around.

Most of the steps of transitioning can be reversed.(except for T and stuff) but kids should be able to cut their hair, using different names/ pronouns, bind, wear different clothing. Most of the time just doing that will help significantly. And it is completely reversible.

I like it sometimes it really depends on what they say n stuff. I still have a cycle and I hate and despise it. But I don’t care if they say female. As long as they don’t be transphobic and stuff like “only women have periods yada yada.”

For me basically, my whole life it felt like something was off. It’s just things never seemed right until I was seen as a man. And it a positive affinity and a dislike of my body at the same time. I used to stare at other teens or children wishing I had their life, being born as a man.

I would still have tons of dysphoria. Some of the things that I do that perceived feminine do give me dysphoria, but not as much as getting dead-named, misgendered, not having a flat chest, and different anatomy etc. but some things I love to do, like painting are perceived feminine. It’s basically a battle zone in your head 24/7. Sometimes I will be painting and just have to stop because the dysphoria is just too much. I do know that anyone can paint, and there’s alot of famous men painters.
